<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par69 />{{GHGheb|text=וִֽירֵשׁ֫וּךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=12}} and {{GHGheb|text=וִֽירֵשׁ֫וּהָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=69|verse=36}}, &c., are most simply explained from the return of this ''ĭ''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|t}}
5. As an exception, the {{GHGterm|imperfect Niphʿal}} sometimes has a {{GHGheb|text=י}} instead of the {{GHGheb|text=ו}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּיָּ֫חֶל|translate=and he stayed}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=12}} (unless the {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} or {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּחֶל}}, as in ver. 10, is to be read), cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=13}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=8}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}.—The first person always has the form {{GHGheb|text=אִוָּשֵׁב}}, not {{GHGheb|text=אֶוָּשֵׁב}}, cf. {{GHGpar|51|p}}.—In the {{GHGterm|participle}} the plural {{GHGheb|text=נוּגֵי}} (from {{GHGheb|text=יָגָה}}, with depression of ''ô'' to ''û'', cf. {{GHGpar|27|n}}) is found in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=3|verse=18}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=4}}. While in these cases some doubt may be felt as to the correctness of the Masoretic pointing, much more is this so in the perfect {{GHGheb|text=נוּלְּדוּ}} ''null<sup>e</sup>dhû'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=3|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=20|verse=8|hidebook=1}}, for {{GHGheb|text=נֽוֹלְדוּ}} which appears to be required by the {{GHGterm|wāw}} in the initial syllable.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|u}}
6. In the {{GHGterm|imperfect Piʿēl}} elision of the first radical ({{GHGheb|text=י}}) sometimes takes place after {{GHGterm|wāw consec.}} (as in the case of {{GHGheb|text=א}}, {{GHGpar|68|k}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּגֶּה}} for {{GHGheb|text=וַיְיַגֶּה|translate=and he has grieved}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=3|verse=33}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּדּוּ}} for {{GHGheb|text=וַיְיַדּוּ|translate=and they have cast}}, verse 53, from {{GHGheb|text=ידה}}, which may also be a true verb {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}} (on the other hand, in {{GHGheb|text=יַדּוּ גוֹרָל|translate=they have cast lots}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=4|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ob|chapter=1|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=10}}, a {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} of {{GHGheb|text=יָדַד}} is required by the context; but as this, being a ''transitive'' perfect, ought to have the form {{GHGheb|text=יָֽדְדוּ}} according to {{GHGpar|67|a}}, perhaps we should read {{GHGheb|text=יִדּוּ}}). So from a verb {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}}, of the second class, {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּבְּשֵׁ֫הוּ}} for {{GHGheb|text=וַיְיַבְּשֵׁ֫הוּ|translate=and he made it dry}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=4}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּשְּׁרֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=32|verse=30}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} (the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} points either to {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיְיַשְּׁרֵם}} or {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּיְשִׁרֵם}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|v}}
7. The {{GHGterm|imperative Hiphʿîl}}, instead of the usual form {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשֵב}}, sometimes has ''î'' in the second syllable; {{GHGheb|text=הוֹצִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=הוֹפִיעַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=94|verse=1}} (before {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, hence probably a mere mistake for {{GHGheb|text=הוֹפִ֫יעָה}}). On the uncertainty of the tone in {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשִׁיעָה־נָּא}} see {{GHGpar|53|m}}. When closed by a guttural the second syllable generally has ''ă'', as {{GHGheb|text=הוֹדַע}}, {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשַׁע}}, cf. also {{GHGheb|text=הֹקַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=17}} (as in the ''infin. constr.'' {{GHGheb|text=הוֹכַח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=26}}; see {{GHGpar|65|f}}). On the other hand, ''î'' always appears when the syllable is open, thus {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשִׁ֫יבָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשִׁ֫יבִי}}, and so also before suffixes ({{GHGpar|61|g}}). {{GHGheb|text=הַיְצֵא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=17}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} ({{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} {{GHGheb|text=הוֹצֵא}}, see {{GHGpar|70|b}}) is irregular.—The {{GHGterm|jussive}} and the ''imperfect consecutive Hiphʿîl'' when the tone is drawn back take {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} in the second syllable, as in {{GHGterm|Qal}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=י֫וֹסֶף|translate=that he may increase}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=5}}, before {{GHGheb|text=לֶ֫קַח}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=28}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=3|verse=26}} after {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיֹּ֫סֶף}} ({{GHGheb|text=תּ֫וֹסְףְּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=6}} is anomalous); in {{GHGterm|pause}}, however, also {{GHGheb|text=תּוֹסַף}} as {{GHGterm|jussive}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=32}} (usual {{GHGterm|jussive}} in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=יוֹשֵׁב}}, &c., which occurs even without the pause after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=24|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=8|verse=4}}, &c.). With a final guttural {{GHGheb|text=יֹדַ֫ע}} and {{GHGheb|text=יוֹכַ֫ח}} ({{GHGterm|jussive}}) and {{GHGheb|text=וַיּוֹכַח}} &c.; with a final {{GHGheb|text=ר}} in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=וַתֹּתַֽר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=14}}: on {{GHGheb|text=וְישַֽׁעֲכֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=35|verse=4}}, cf. {{GHGpar|65|f}}).—On forms like {{GHGheb|text=יְהוֹשִׁיעַ}}, see {{GHGpar|53|q}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|w}}
In ''Hophʿal ô'' stands instead of {{GHGheb|text=וּ}}, in {{GHGheb|text=הוֹדַע}} (for {{GHGheb|text=הוּדַע}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=4|verse=23.28}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֹגָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=13}}, and perhaps in {{GHGheb|text=יוֹרֶא}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יוּרֶה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=11|verse=25}}; but cf. Delitzsch on the passage.—''Ptcp.'' {{GHGheb|text=מוּדַ֫עַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=12|verse=5}} ''Q<sup>e</sup>re'' ({{GHGheb|text=מְיֻדַּ֫עַת}} ''K<sup>e</sup>th'').—An {{GHGterm|infinitive Hophʿal}} with feminine ending occurs in {{GHGheb|text=הֻלֶּ֫דֶת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=20}}, for {{GHGheb|text=הֻלֶ֫דֶת}}={{GHGheb|text=הוּל׳}}; cf. above, t, on {{GHGheb|text=נוּלְּדוּ}}, and § 71 at the end.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|x}}
8. The verb {{GHGheb|text=הָלַךְ|translate=to go}}, also belongs in some respects to the {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} class, since it forms (as if from {{GHGheb|text=וָלַךְ}}) {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יֵלֵךְ}}, with {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּ֫לֶךְ}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּלַֽךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=61}}, &c.), 1st sing. {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֵלֵךְ}} (but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֵלַ֑ךְ}}); {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} {{GHGheb|text=לֶ֫כֶת}} with suff. {{GHGheb|text=לֶכְתִּי}} ({{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} under the influence of the following palatal, as in {{GHGheb|text=נֶכְדִּי}}, cf. also {{GHGheb|text=נֶגְדִּי}}); {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=לֵךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=לֶךְ־}}, in the lengthened form {{GHGheb|text=לְכָה}} (as an interjection referring even to a ''feminine'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=32}}, or a ''plural'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=44}}) and {{GHGheb|text=לְךָ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=25|verse=17}}); ''Hiph.'' {{GHGheb|text=הוֹלִיךְ}} (also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=הוֹלִ֫יכִי}} 2nd ''fem. imperative'' is to be read for {{GHGheb|text=הֵילִ֫יכִי}}, which probably arose merely through<section end=par69 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
